column1: # Columns: pinyin <TAB> expected first choice <TAB> weight
#   * pinyin   the `'`-separated toneless syllable key, in the canonical
#   * expected the word a user typing that key expects at the head of the
#   * weight   the relative importance of the row, taken from the word list's
#              own frequency column. The plain hit rate counts every row once;
#              the weighted rate counts a row this many times.
# The set is hand-written and is never generated. It is read by `xtask tune`
# (the weight grid search) and by the decode tests. Rows whose key is ambiguous
# are deliberate: they are the rows a scoring change can move, and a set of keys
# with a single candidate each would measure nothing. Blank lines and lines
# ── two syllables, several words share the key ─────────────────────────────
# The baseline composition of 银行 reads the second character as `xing`; the
# correction table gives it the reading the word actually has. A lexicon that
# composes keys from the L1 table alone cannot serve this row, so `xtask tune`
# reports it as one unreachable row; the compiled dictionary can.
